subject: Order Form: pricing bands, commit thresholds & invoicing flow
messages:
From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@lobent.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: mark.chen@lobent.com
Date: Mon, 27 Oct 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order Form: pricing bands, commit thresholds & invoicing flow

Hi Rafael / Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Lobent is excited to move toward a pilot. Attached is our redline to the Order Form (Lobent_OrderForm_v2_redline.pdf) plus a simple payment cadence we sketched (payment_schedule.xlsx). High-level items we need to confirm before procurement will sign: 

1) Pricing bands: we want to ensure the unit price steps are linked to the committed ARR bands (you'll see comments on pages 3-4).
2) Minimum commit definition and true-up: procurement is asking for a clear math example and a 30-day true-up window after quarter close.
3) Net terms: standard for us is Net60; we understand Redwood typically runs Net45 or Net30 — can you confirm flexibility?
4) Invoicing cadence and invoice recipient: we'd like invoices to go to AP@lobent.com; can you accept PO routing to a US entity?
5) Taxes: for EU sales we need clarity on VAT handling and withholding responsibilities for services.

Can Kimberly and your finance/legal team review the attached redline and let us know which items will require MSA-level changes vs order-form only?

If it helps, Mark (cc'd) is our procurement lead and can join a short call.

Best,

Sara Liu
Head of Procurement
Lobent Systems
[sent with attachment: Lobent_OrderForm_v2_redline.pdf (PDF, 312 KB); payment_schedule.xlsx (XLSX, 24 KB)]

From: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@lobent.com>, Mark Chen <mark.chen@lobent.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 27 Oct 2025 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order Form: pricing bands, commit thresholds & invoicing flow

Sara / Mark — thanks for the redline and the payment cadence. Rafael here from commercial; looping in Kimberly (commercial/legal) and Ben (finance/ops) to help close the items you listed. Quick summary so we can align internally: 

- Pricing bands: we can map the unit price tiers to the ARR bands shown, but need to confirm the effective date for banding (sign date vs first invoice).
- Minimum commit / true-up: Redwood typically does quarter-based true-ups with a 30-day invoice window; the MSA doesn't need to change if the Order Form specifies the mechanics, but flagged if Lobent wants to change liability caps.
- Net terms: Ben, can we confirm whether Net60 is feasible for Lobent or if approval required from RevOps?
- Invoicing routing: fine to route to AP@lobent.com; we will need the PO number and remit-to entity (Ben: see attachment request).
- Taxes: Kimberly, please confirm the recommendation for VAT vs customer withholding and what evidence Lobent must provide (W-9 vs VAT reg).

Proposed next steps: Kimberly to provide redline callouts (order-form vs MSA), Ben to confirm net terms exception path and what finance docs we need, then 30-min call with Lobent to finalize. Are you available for a call this Thursday (30 Oct) or Friday?

Rafael
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

[Attachment: forwarded Lobent_OrderForm_v2_redline.pdf referenced for internal review]

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@lobent.com>, Mark Chen <mark.chen@lobent.com>
Cc: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 29 Oct 2025 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order Form: pricing bands, commit thresholds & invoicing flow

Sara / Mark — thanks for the redline. I reviewed both attachments and have the following commercial/legal responses (order-form level where possible; MSA change only if Lobent requires different risk allocation):

1) Pricing bands: we can accept banded pricing tied to committed ARR, effective from the Start Date instead of sign date. Please confirm you accept start-date indexing (this avoids retrospective pricing changes).

2) Minimum commit and true-up: we propose the Order Form specify (a) committed units per quarter, (b) true-up calculation within 30 days of quarter close, and (c) an overage billing mechanism at the next higher band for over-usage. We added a worked example in payment_schedule.xlsx. This can stay in Order Form — no MSA edit needed.

3) Net terms: Redwood standard is Net45. Net60 is an exception that requires RevOps + Finance sign-off and an approved credit check. If Lobent needs Net60 we can run a credit review and (if approved) amend the Order Form's payment terms; otherwise Net45 will be the default.

4) Invoicing routing / PO: we can route invoices to AP@lobent.com but need a remit-to legal entity (US entity name and EIN or EU VAT ID) to determine whether VAT applies. If Lobent intends to use an EU entity, we will require VAT registration evidence before zero-rating VAT.

5) Taxes / withholding: for cross-border services, Redwood is responsible for assessing VAT on invoices based on the billed entity and country. Withholding tax liability remains the customer's responsibility unless otherwise agreed and documented in the Order Form. If Lobent requests vendor-side withholding relief, provide a tax residency certificate.

6) Escrow / service credits: I noted Lobent removed the standard SLA credits clause. If Lobent requires removal of SLA credits that is a material MSA change; propose we keep SLA credits but can cap exposure in the Order Form.

Action items from our side:
- Ben to confirm whether Finance can approve conditional Net60 (ben: see payment_schedule.xlsx sample).
- Rafael to confirm Start Date vs sign date indexing with Lobent.

Please see my inline comments in Lobent_OrderForm_v2_redline.pdf for exact sentence-level edits. Happy to join a call — Thursday looks tight for me but Friday 10–11am PT works.

Thanks,

Kimberly Park
Head of Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
[kimberly_park@redwood.ai]
[Attachment referenced: payment_schedule.xlsx (worked example)]

From: Mark Chen <mark.chen@lobent.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: Sara Liu <sara.liu@lobent.com>, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 03 Nov 2025 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order Form: pricing bands, commit thresholds & invoicing flow

Kimberly / Rafael / Ben — thanks for the quick review and the worked example. A few final points from Lobent procurement/finance: 

- Net terms: Lobent's standard corporate policy is Net60. We understand this is an exception; can Redwood provisionally accept Net60 pending the credit check? If so, we will provide the contact for the credit reviewer and a copy of our latest audited financials.

- Remit-to/legal entity: we will route invoices to Lobent Systems, Inc. (EIN: 12-3456789) for US invoices. For EU invoices Lobent will provide VAT registration numbers per-entity.

- SLA credits: Lobent prefers to remove SLA credits from the Order Form and rely on service termination remedies in the MSA. If Redwood needs SLA credits retained, can we agree to a capped exposure (suggest cap = 3% of the quarterly invoice)?

- AP contact and PO: please send a test invoice to AP@lobent.com and we will confirm PO exposure and routing.

We can accept Friday 10:30am PT for a short call to finalize items and then circulate a DocuSign link. If you can provisionally accept Net60 subject to credit, we'll expedite procurement.

—Mark
Procurement Lead | Lobent Systems
